title: signal-fencing-client-abort-edge-reconnect-policy-openai-compat
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: Production customers continue to hit intermittent tailcases when clients disconnect mid-stream or issue a cancel while the server is still reconciling long-running tool calls. This leads to 'zombie' leases on backend resources, double-tool-invocations after reconnects, and confusing metrics spikes. This PR introduces a signal-fencing model paired with an edge-side reconnect policy to ensure client cancels and disconnects are handled deterministically while preserving OpenAI-compatible streaming semantics. Design summary: 1) Signal fencing: a short-lived fencing token is issued per streaming session lease. When a client sends a cancel/abort or disconnect occurs, the token moves the session into a quarantined state for a configurable grace window (default 30s). The server will honor idempotent tool-call markers only if the token is active; reconnects negotiate a fresh token plus an optional continuation handle. 2) Edge reconnect policy: the edge proxy supports a three-stage reconnect state machine (ACCEPT, QUARANTINE, REJECT) driven by lease expiry and backend load signals. Clients attempting to reconnect during QUARANTINE receive structured instructions (JSON payload) indicating whether to resume, re-request, or start a new session. 3) Tool/function calling semantics: function/tool invocations are gated by an invocation-id + token pair; duplicate requests outside the token window are rejected to prevent double-execution. 4) OpenAI adapter compatibility: kept existing streaming frames unchanged; the adapter injects a compatible control frame type ("x-control-signal") that downstream OpenAI-compat clients will ignore if not understood. 5) Rollout: feature-flag default off for hosted; enabled for dedicated/private on request for initial customers. Backwards compatibility: clients that don't understand the control frame will continue to operate normally; tool idempotency is strongly recommended but not required to adopt immediately. Implementation highlights: - server: src/server/streaming/orchestrator.py implements session fencing and state transitions, includes new metrics (fenced_sessions, resume_requests, quarantine(evictions)). - runtime: src/server/streaming/lease_manager.rs adds compact lease fingerprints and lease negotiation RPCs to support quick fencing checks. - adapter: api/openai/stream_adapter.go maps the new control frame to the OpenAI-compatible stream envelope. - client docs and examples: docs/api/streaming-lifecycle.md and examples/ts/reconnect-guides.md show recommended client backoff and token negotiation. Testing: new integration tests tests/integration/stream_quarantine_test.py simulate disconnects during in-flight tool invocations and assert single-execution and correct client instructions. Security/ops: KMS-backed token signing added so fences cannot be spoofed; audit logs now capture fence transitions. Release notes: see field below. This description string is continuous and contains checklist, design, testing, and rollout guidance for reviewers.

release_notes: Added session fencing and edge-side reconnect policy to make streaming cancels and disconnects deterministic. Default off behind feature flag for hosted; opt-in for Dedicated/Private. Adds fence metrics, KMS-backed token signing (enterprise opt-in), and non-breaking OpenAI-compatible control frames. Recommended client changes: honor control frame ignore semantics, include invocation-id for tool calls.
